def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison.text: The formal composition vector of a compound records, for each primitive label $c$, the sum of its positive scale coefficients. Two compounds have the same composition exactly when these vectors agree. The distinct **formal mass** $m(A)$ is the sum of all scale coefficients in $A$, a dimensionless bookkeeping quantity; it is not physical mass in kilograms, mole amount, energy, or volume. Same-composition compounds have equal formal mass. For states $A,B$ of the same compound type, write $A\prec B$ when the declared adiabatic-accessibility relation of [[def-td-adiabatic-accessibility]] admits that endpoint comparison. This definition does not infer accessibility from coordinate addition.

post-td-accessibility-a1-a6.text: physical_scope: Adopted order assumptions for adiabatic accessibility on equal-formal-mass finite compounds in the declared family, including cross-type comparisons only when a channel network later admits them; they do not establish that an actual material family satisfies them.

Use the fully scalable model family of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]: every positive scale map is defined on the full state domain, finite separated state spaces are full products, and nested scaling has the declared reversible preparation transport. These additional existence and transport assumptions are not supplied by the general partial-domain bulk postulate. Adopt the following axioms for $\prec$ on every declared pair of finite compounds with equal formal mass in [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]. Initially this covers equal-composition adiabatic accessibility. If a later channel model admits comparisons between distinct composition types, the same axioms apply to those comparisons and all their finite scaled products; no cross-type transition is admitted by this postulate alone. They are assumptions of the operational model, not consequences of the process definition or of energy additivity.

rem-td-entropy-construction-hypotheses.text: The order relation in [[def-td-adiabatic-accessibility]] is a model-defined relation between equilibrium endpoints; it is not a measured trajectory law. A1–A6, A7, S1–S3, T1–T5 and C1 are adopted physical assumptions. The contact-product conclusion is conditional on the full list. In the inspected Lieb–Yngvason source, Theorem 4.8 is stated under T1–T4; the local supplier’s proof branch explicitly also needs the universal range T5 and the separate join-coherence bridge C1. The bare printed source interface does not discharge those stronger inputs.

def-td-adiabatic-accessibility.text: Fix a material constitution $c$ and its equilibrium state domain $D_c$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Use the protocol functional $Q:\mathcal P_s\to\mathbb R$ (values in joules) supplied by [[def-td-process-and-protocol]] on all admitted records; its existence on this full class does not extend the core-only energy-balance law. For $x,y\in D_c$, write $x\prec_c y$, and say that $y$ is adiabatically accessible from $x$, exactly when the declared process model admits at least one record $P\in\mathcal P_s$ from [[def-td-process-and-protocol]] with $x_P^-=x$, $x_P^+=y$, $Q[P]=0$, and the model’s stated auxiliary and work-device endpoint conditions satisfied. The material constitution is the same at both endpoints. The process record must account for the selected outer boundary and every auxiliary included by its protocol.

The sign convention is $Q>0$ into the system and $W_{\mathrm{on}}>0$ for work done on it, as fixed in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. Thus adiabatic means zero protocol-assigned heat, not zero work, zero energy change, isolation, quasistatic evolution, or reversibility. The relation concerns equilibrium endpoints only; intermediate configurations may be nonequilibrium. Existence of a witness record is model input, not a consequence of this definition.

Fix the outer-boundary record $b_s$ of that system and take $\mathcal B_\alpha=\{b_s\}$. The embedding

def-td-reservoir-cycle.text: Fix a working system $s$ of constitution $c$ and a closed process record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ with equilibrium endpoints as in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. A cycle of the working system is such a record with $x_P^-=x_P^+$; the reservoirs and work store need not return to their initial energy states.

A two-reservoir cycle consists of one working-system cycle, two labelled baths $h,c$ at fixed temperatures $T_h,T_c>0$, and the ideal work store. The labels specify the transfer roles below; the general bookkeeping permits equal or reversed positive bath temperatures. In the strictly ordered subfamily $0<T_c<T_h$, call $h$ the hot bath and $c$ the cold bath. The engine-efficiency and refrigerator bounds use this subfamily. No existence of a cycle with prescribed transfer signs is asserted. They lie inside one isolated outer boundary in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]], so the full compound has no external matter or energy transfer. There are no unlisted heat, work, matter, kinetic-energy, or external-potential-energy changes. The admitted process and transfer signs are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]].

For use of [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]], the model supplies an admitted core closed process record $P_{\mathrm{tot}}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s_{\mathrm{tot}})$ for this full compound $s_{\mathrm{tot}}$. In particular, it supplies the compound's fixed positive mass and defined endpoint center-of-mass velocities in its fixed bookkeeping chart, as required by [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. Its two endpoint configurations lie in the declared equilibrium set of that process model, its separately tracked center-of-mass kinetic and external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change, and its endpoint association $\rho_{P_{\mathrm{tot}}}:\{-,+\}\to\mathcal F$ has both values in the same feasible set $\mathcal F$ from that postulate. In the constituent ordering of $\rho_{P_{\mathrm{tot}}}(\pm)$, the working-system state is $x_P^\pm$ and the bath and work-store components have the corresponding energy coordinates $E_h^\pm,E_c^\pm,E_w^\pm$. The total-compound record and the working-system record therefore have matching working-system endpoints; all bath and work-store energy differences below refer to these same total-compound endpoint tuples. The former record is the input to the second-law postulate, and $P$ is the working-system record to which the first-law balance applies.

def-td-reversible-process.text: Let $P=(I_P,x_P^-,x_P^+,z_P,\kappa_P,r_P)$ be an admitted closed process record as defined in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with equilibrium endpoints $x_P^-,x_P^+\in D_c$. The record is **reversible relative to its declared boundary and protocol** when the model also admits a reverse record $P^{\mathrm{rev}}$ for the same system and material constitution, starting at $x_P^+$ and ending at $x_P^-$, such that every auxiliary and device state specified by the protocol is restored to its initial state and every signed boundary transfer is reversed. In particular,

def-td-thermal-contact-constraints.text: Fix two members $a=(c_A,x_A)$ and $b=(c_B,x_B)$, named constituents $A,B$ of those constitutions, and a declared contact-protocol convention. A **thermal-contact protocol** is an admitted preparation/process record $P$ of their compound system $A\sqcup B$, with the configuration curve $z_P:I_P\to Z_{A\sqcup B}$ and equilibrium endpoint configurations specified in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The contact model supplies constituent endpoint-coordinate maps

and requires $\xi_A(z_P(t_0))=x_A$ and $\xi_B(z_P(t_0))=x_B$. These constituent maps are additional declared model data; they are not inferred from the compound's coordinate tuple. Write $x_A^+=\xi_A(z_P(t_1))$ and $x_B^+=\xi_B(z_P(t_1))$ for the constituent final coordinates. The two constituents are separated by a declared diathermal contact: matter transfer and mechanical or composition work across that contact are forbidden, while the protocol permits thermal energy transfer between the constituents. The compound's external boundary and all retained constraints are specified as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]] and [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. No continuity or differentiability of the configuration curve is added here.

Let $\mathcal P_T(A,B)$ be the set of contact records admitted by the fixed convention. The model supplies an internal transfer map $q_{A\to B}:\mathcal P_T(A,B)\to\mathbb R$, whose values are numerical magnitudes in joules: $q_{A\to B}[P]>0$ means net thermal energy transferred from $A$ to $B$ across this contact during $I_P$. Set $q_{B\to A}[P]:=-q_{A\to B}[P]$. Zero net internal heat transfer means exactly $q_{A\to B}[P]=0$; it does not assert zero transfer at every intermediate time. This map is additional protocol data, distinct from the compound's external-boundary map $Q$ in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. In particular, an isolated compound may have nonzero $q_{A\to B}$ while its external $Q$ is zero. Identifying this internal map with constituent heat records requires separately supplied constituent records and consistent boundary assignments.

For each tested ordered pair $(a,b)$, the convention specifies one admitted contact preparation $P_{a,b}\in\mathcal P_T(A,B)$ with the initial coordinates above, and a subset $\mathcal E_T(A,B)\subseteq\mathcal P_T(A,B)$ designated as equilibrium contact preparations. These are model inputs, not an equilibration theorem. The pair is in **thermal contact equilibrium**, written $a\sim_T b$, exactly when its selected record $P_{a,b}$ belongs to $\mathcal E_T(A,B)$, has $x_A^+=x_A$ and $x_B^+=x_B$, and satisfies $q_{A\to B}[P_{a,b}]=0$. Untested pairs are not in the relation. This criterion is protocol-dependent: changing the selected preparation or retained constraints can change the relation. For fixed constitutions, coordinate notation $x_A\sim_T x_B$ abbreviates $(c_A,x_A)\sim_T(c_B,x_B)$ using the two specified tag embeddings. It does not define a relation on untagged coordinates across unspecified material types. The relation is defined only on the stated family $\mathcal T$ and for the declared contact protocols. This definition does not assert that $\sim_T$ is reflexive, symmetric, or transitive, and it does not assign a real-valued temperature to its equivalence classes. Lieb–Yngvason §IV.A instead defines thermal equilibrium using adiabatic equivalence with a thermal join; the present record-based criterion is a separately adopted convention.

ex-td-clapeyron-linear-branches.text: for $i\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$, with $s_\alpha=2\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $s_\beta=5\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $v_\alpha=1.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, and $v_\beta=4.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$. Set $G_i=n_i g_i$ and use the natural Gibbs assignments $S_i=-\partial_TG_i$, $V_i=\partial_pG_i$, $\mu_i=\partial_{n_i}G_i$, and $U_i=G_i+TS_i-pV_i$. Thus same-tag homogeneity is explicit. Assume the constructed model stipulates an attained coexistence endpoint with energy, volume, and species pairwise transfer curves feasible for all sufficiently small increments of either sign while every nonselected phase and auxiliary coordinate is fixed, and a reversible $\alpha\to\beta$ conversion in contact with an ideal thermal reservoir at $T_0$. The reversible conversion is a record of the complete finite isolated compound comprising converted phases, the fixed-temperature reservoir, work stores and all auxiliaries, with equilibrium endpoints and additive component entropy. The forward and reverse complete-compound records are admitted in the core closed class of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], each with a supplied positive total mass, defined endpoint center-of-mass velocities in its fixed Galilean chart, and zero endpoint changes of compound center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field energies. Every component other than the converted phases and reservoir has zero entropy change, and the reservoir change is $-Q/T_0$. These are the exact additional entropy premises of the local Clapeyron theorem. These parameters and endpoint assumptions are model inputs, not empirical claims.

ex-td-irreversible-adiabatic-compression.text: title: Entropy increase in an idealized adiabatic compression
deps: [def-td-process-and-protocol, def-td-reversible-process, def-td-si-quantities, post-td-first-law-energy, post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy, def-natural-logarithm, thm-natural-logarithm-laws]
- title: Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §2.6, ideal-gas entropy and adiabatic examples

for positive reference values $T_0$ in K and $V_0$ in $\mathrm{m^3}$. At initial equilibrium let $T_i>0$ and $V_i>0$. A piston protocol suddenly raises the external pressure from the initial value $p_i$ to a constant final load $p_f$, compresses the gas adiabatically to $V_f=(9/10)V_i$, and dissipatively settles it to a final equilibrium state. The protocol admits no reverse record, so it is irreversible by [[def-td-reversible-process]]. The idealization assumes no change in the included load's entropy; all numerical behavior is a model assumption and deduction, not an empirical measurement.
**Given:** The process and sign conventions of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], the closed-record first-law postulate [[post-td-first-law-energy]], and the stated ideal-gas model.
[F1] A process record is adiabatic exactly when $Q[P]=0$; $W_{\mathrm{on}}>0$ denotes work done on the system ([[def-td-process-and-protocol]]).

[A2] The gas is the system inside the declared outer boundary: no matter crosses it, its material constitution is fixed, and its mechanical model supplies a total mass $M>0$ and center-of-mass velocities in the fixed chart of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The gas center of mass is at rest at both endpoint preparations, so $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}=0$; no separately tracked external-field potential energy changes (the model may take that term to be absent), so $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$. Thus the admitted record is in $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ as defined by [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. Its protocol has $Q[P]=0$, a constant external load $p_f$ during compression, and $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]=p_f(V_i-V_f)$. The final equilibrium obeys $p_fV_f=nRT_f$, and the initial equilibrium obeys $p_iV_i=nRT_i$. The apparatus is stipulated to dissipatively settle and to have zero entropy change.

ex-td-nonzero-isothermal-work-loop.text: where $C>0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $U_*>0$ is in joules, $a>0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $b>0$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, and $S_0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Let $s$ be a closed system of this constitution and amount. Stipulate that the process model admits a record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ as in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], using one fixed Galilean inertial chart and satisfying $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}=\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$. Its equilibrium state path is piecewise-C1, starting at $(T_1,V_1)$ and following, in order, a constant-temperature leg $T=T_1$ from $V_1$ to $V_2$, a constant-volume leg $V=V_2$ to $T_2$, a constant-temperature leg $T=T_2$ from $V_2$ to $V_1$, and a constant-volume leg $V=V_1$ back to $T_1$, where $T_1>T_2>0$ and $0<V_1<V_2<1/b$. The moving boundary is a planar piston of constant area. Throughout the volume-changing legs it remains in frictionless mechanical equilibrium with a load tracking the equilibrium pressure, as required by [[post-td-mechanical-conjugate-identification]]; controlled heat exchange is permitted, and no other work coordinate acts. In this model, the finite work transfer $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$ is defined as the line integral of the incremental piston work along this piecewise-C1 path. This is a stipulated idealized model record, not a reported observation. Its pressure-work integral is not an endpoint increment.

post-td-first-law-energy.text: Here the internal-energy coordinate is evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], while $Q[P]$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$ are the protocol transfers defined by [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], in joules as in [[def-td-si-quantities]]. The sign convention is positive $Q$ into the system and positive $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ for work done on it. If $P$ is adiabatic, its defining condition is $Q[P]=0$, so the same adopted balance gives $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]=U_c(x_P^+)-U_c(x_P^-)$.

The process record and the zero-change conditions are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The process may pass through nonequilibrium configurations; this postulate compares endpoint entropies only and assigns no entropy function to those intermediate configurations.

For an admitted reversible operation in the sense of [[def-td-reversible-process]], adopt $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(+))-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(-))=0$. An admitted irreversible adiabatic operation may have a strictly positive entropy increase, but strict increase is not required for every irreversible operation. The postulate does not state monotonicity for an open compound, an externally driven process, a subsystem that exchanges energy with an omitted environment, or every microscopic trajectory.

post-td-unattainability-scoped.text: Let $\mathcal U_c$ be the model-declared set of cooling controls, and let $\mathcal C\subseteq\overline D_c\times\overline D_c\times\mathcal U_c\times(0,\infty)$ be the model's full declared family of admitted cooling operation records. Each record $\gamma=(x^-,x^+,u,\tau)$ has initial-endpoint map $i(\gamma)=x^-$, final-endpoint map $f(\gamma)=x^+$, control $u\in\mathcal U_c$, and finite positive duration $\tau(\gamma)=\tau$ seconds. Its positive-temperature portions obey the process conventions of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], while the model separately declares how a boundary endpoint in $D_0$ is represented. Define two records to be compatible exactly when $f(\gamma)=i(\gamma')$. A finite protocol is a tuple $(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m)$ for $m\in\mathbb N$, $m\ge1$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), with each successive pair compatible; its initial and final endpoints are $i(\gamma_1)$ and $f(\gamma_m)$, and its duration is $\sum_{j=1}^m\tau(\gamma_j)$. Let $\mathcal P_{\mathcal C}$ be the set of all such finite protocols and let $\mathcal P_{\mathcal C}^{+}:=\{p\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal C}:i(p)\in D_{c,+}\}$. For each $p=(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m)$, define $i(p):=i(\gamma_1)$, $f(p):=f(\gamma_m)$, and $\tau(p):=\sum_{j=1}^m\tau(\gamma_j)<\infty$. For a nonvacuous application, require $\mathcal P_{\mathcal C}^{+}\ne\varnothing$ and declare $\mathcal C$ as the full operation family rather than defining it to exclude boundary endpoints. Define $\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathcal C}:=\{(i(p),f(p)):p\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal C}\}\subseteq\overline D_c\times\overline D_c$.

pthm-td-fixed-tp-reaction-potential-mini.text: Let $P_s\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ be an admitted closed system process record as defined in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with system endpoints $x_{P_s}^-,x_{P_s}^+\in D_c$. Let $R$ be its ideal thermal reservoir and $B$ its ideal pressure store; both lie inside a declared isolated-compound outer boundary. Let $\widehat P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s\sqcup R\sqcup B)$ be an admitted core closed process record for that isolated compound, whose supplied total mass is positive, whose endpoint center-of-mass velocities are defined in one fixed Galilean chart, and whose compound center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change. These are conditions on the whole compound, additional to the system-record conditions. By an extension, require that $\widehat P$ has the same time interval, system endpoints, system configuration path, and system-side protocol and transfer records as $P_s$, together with the reservoir and store records. Write its compound endpoint association as

[F1] [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]: $P_s$ is one admitted closed system process record with endpoints $x_{P_s}^\pm$; its protocol assigns the same record's heat and work functionals $Q[P_s]$ and $W_{\rm on}[P_s]$ in joules. The isolated-compound record $\widehat P$ records the auxiliary endpoint states and extension of that system record.

pthm-td-reservoir-minimum-principles.text: [A3] The system and bath, with the pressure store when present, form a complete isolated compound with fixed total energy. In the fixed-volume case $\Delta U+\Delta E_R=0$; in the fixed-pressure case $\Delta U+\Delta E_R+p_0\Delta V=0$. These system energy balances are adopted ideal-environment constraints. Each operation includes an admitted core closed record of the complete compound as in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with positive fixed total mass, defined endpoint center-of-mass velocities in one fixed Galilean chart, and zero endpoint changes of compound center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field energies. The model supplies the full constituent and auxiliary endpoint sets with their energy and entropy maps, and an endpoint association $\rho_P:\{-,+\}\to\mathcal F$ into one exact feasible set, representing both aggregate equilibrium endpoints and their system, bath and store coordinates. Every named auxiliary is retained; the endpoint split is admitted by the additive rule required by [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]. Any additional retained auxiliary has constant total energy and entropy contributions throughout $\mathcal F$. On every tuple of $\mathcal F$, total energy is one fixed constant and total entropy is the sum of the system, bath and constant store or other entropy-neutral contributions. In the fixed-pressure case require $E_p-p_0V=C_p$ on every tuple of that same $\mathcal F$ for one fixed constant $C_p$; at fixed volume $V$ is fixed and the pressure store is absent. Thus the constraints used for global minimization hold throughout the feasible set, including disconnected components. No core-record assumption is imposed on the subsystem alone: its displayed energy balances are already adopted above.

pthm-td-useful-work-bound.text: **Given:** A system $\sigma$ of fixed constitution $c$, an admitted record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(\sigma)$ with equilibrium endpoints $x_i,x_f$, $T_0>0$, $p_0>0$, and the ideal reservoir/work-store model below. The core-record conditions and fixed-chart bookkeeping are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. Write $Q=Q[P]$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}=W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$. Use $W_{\mathrm{out}}>0$ for energy delivered by the system, in joules.
[F3] [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]: $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are process-record transfers, not state functions; an adiabatic record has $Q=0$.

cex-td-degenerate-thermometer-comparison.text: [F1] [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]: product states are tagged scaled copies and product comparison is the declared relation, not coordinate addition.

def-td-cross-type-reaction-network.text: independently of a nonunique factorization. These are explicit admissibility and calibration conditions of the declared model, not consequences of a channel record or claims that every physical network satisfies them. Separated products remain sums of represented states; the distinct raw tags of scaled and joined types are retained, with reversible preparation transport as specified in [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], rather than identifying those tags. The dimensioned endpoint-quantity maps and channel balance predicates remain the separately supplied physical data. In addition, each channel must preserve the dimensionless formal mass $m$ of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]; this is the equal-coefficient-mass convention required by the mathematical chain-cost supplier, not a statement that formal mass is kilograms or moles. The common relation on all equal-formal-mass compounds satisfies A1–A6 of [[post-td-accessibility-a1-a6]], including consistency with spectators and stability. ex-td-local-equilibrium-profile.text: title: A nonconstant local-equilibrium temperature field

For the homogeneous comparison cell, supply $\mathcal X=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ with states $(e,y)$, physical energy $(1\,\mathrm J)e$, and numerical entropy $s(e,y)=\ln e-y^2$, where $\ln:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the natural logarithm of [[def-natural-logarithm]] and physical entropy is $(1\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}})s(e,y)$. The coordinate $y$ is dimensionless. Set $r=1$, $C(e,y)=e$, $c(a)=a$, and $B_a=\mathcal X$ for every $a\in\mathcal Z$, so the fixed-energy admissible set is $A_a=\{(a,y):y\in\mathbb R\}$. Its entropy-maximizing set is $E_a=\{(a,0)\}$. Define $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{eq}}=\bigcup_{a>0}E_a$ and supply $q(a)=(a,0)$; assign this comparison state temperature $(1\,\mathrm K)a$. Stipulate the local-equilibrium approximation with this map, so the local constitutive state at $(\mathbf x,t)$ is $q(z(\mathbf x,t))$. The field is static and nonconstant; this stipulation is a model assumption, not an assertion that a physical sample realizes the profile.
**Given:** The local-field convention of [[rem-td-local-equilibrium-branch]] and the parameters just specified.

[F1] [[rem-td-local-equilibrium-branch]]: the local-state field has the displayed domain and its components have continuous first spatial and time partial derivatives; a temperature component is read in kelvins.

[F2] [[rem-td-local-equilibrium-branch]]: an entropy-based local-equilibrium model supplies cell states, entropy, retained constraints and conserved-value maps; $E_a$ is the entropy-maximizing subset of $A_a=\{e\in B_a:C(e)=c(a)\}$, and the supplied map must satisfy $q(a)\in E_a$. Its pointwise comparison state is $q(z(\mathbf x,t))$; attainment is verified for the supplied model rather than inferred from a label.
[F3] [[rem-td-local-equilibrium-branch]]: nonconstant temperature fields are permitted in this continuum model and do not describe global equilibrium.

2.1 For each $a>0$, [A1] gives $A_a=\{(a,y):y\in\mathbb R\}$ and $s(a,0)-s(a,y)=y^2\ge0$, with equality exactly at $y=0$. Thus $E_a=\{(a,0)\}$ and $q(a)\in E_a$, meeting the constrained-maximum criterion in [F2]. The logarithm is finite since $a>0$. By [F1] and step 1.1, the one-coordinate field has the declared range and regularity, so its supplied comparison state is $q(z(\mathbf x,t))$. Steps 1.1–1.2 show that its temperature component is positive and spatially nonconstant; [F3] says this need not describe global equilibrium. No dynamics or experimental outcome is inferred.
